question: Where does the sternocleidomastoid muscle insert?

options.A: Mandible
options.B: Mastoid process
options.C: Sternum
options.D: Clavicle only

explanation: The sternocleidomastoid anchors from the sternum and clavicle up to the mastoid process of the temporal bone. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of keeping antenatal records in a clinic?

options.A: To calculate the monthly financial revenue of the hospital
options.B: To replace verbal communication entirely among staff
options.C: To provide a continuous medical history for safe care
options.D: To fulfill government tax obligations for health workers

explanation: Antenatal records track the progress of pregnancy over time so any healthcare provider can review past findings and make safe clinical decisions. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of giving a structured handover to the postnatal ward staff?

options.A: To clear the delivery room for the next incoming mother
options.B: To verify that all hospital equipment has been returned
options.C: To hand over legal responsibility for the delivery documentation
options.D: To ensure continuity of observation and patient safety

explanation: A structured handover communicates important risk factors and care details so the postnatal team can monitor the mother and baby safely. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T3#BMP212_U3_T3_h6)

question: How can past surgeries like dilation and curettage (D&C) lead to cervical incompetence?

options.A: They damage the collagen and connective tissue of the cervix
options.B: They cause strong, constant contractions of the womb
options.C: They trigger too much progesterone production early on
options.D: They permanently block the hormonal pathways of the placenta

explanation: Surgical procedures on the cervix can harm the tough collagen fibers, making it harder for the cervix to stay closed in future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why do grieving parents often direct angry outbursts at healthcare providers?

options.A: Hospital rules require patients to shout
options.B: Anger is an outward mask for deep pain and helplessness
options.C: Midwives intentionally cause complications
options.D: Anger proves the patient has accepted the loss

explanation: When people feel completely powerless over a tragic outcome, internal agony often spills out as anger toward anyone nearby. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is a primary obstetric cause of acute kidney injury in low-resource settings?

options.A: Severe postpartum haemorrhage
options.B: Eating excessive sugary foods
options.C: Lack of calcium supplements
options.D: Sleeping in poorly ventilated rooms

explanation: Uncontrolled bleeding leads to profound hypovolaemic shock, starving the kidneys of blood flow and causing acute tubular injury. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h5)

question: Which lung volume can NEVER be measured directly using a standard handheld spirometer?

options.A: Inspiratory reserve volume
options.B: Tidal volume
options.C: Residual volume
options.D: Expiratory reserve volume

explanation: Residual volume stays inside the lungs even after blowing out as much air as possible, so it cannot be exhaled into a basic device. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which teaching method works best for training student midwives to repair an episiotomy before working on real patients?

options.A: A large hall lecture on health history
options.B: A silent written reading assignment
options.C: An independent library research essay
options.D: Clinical simulation and demonstration

explanation: Hands-on demonstration and simulation allow students to practice psychomotor skills safely before performing them on mothers. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h5)

question: When is it generally safe to start advancing a postoperative patient from sips of water to solid food?

options.A: When bowel sounds return and flatus is passed
options.B: Immediately after the patient wakes from anesthesia
options.C: When the patient requests a full meal
options.D: Only after the surgical drain has been removed

explanation: The return of bowel sounds and passage of gas indicate that the gastrointestinal tract is waking up from anesthesia. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T6#BMP125_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which shoulder is normally delivered first during a normal vaginal birth?

options.A: The posterior shoulder
options.B: Whichever shoulder is closest to the sacrum
options.C: The anterior shoulder
options.D: Both shoulders deliver at the exact same time

explanation: Gentle downward traction brings the anterior shoulder out from beneath the pubic bone first. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T2#BMP212_U3_T2_h4)

question: When preparing a post-operative bed for a client returning from major abdominal surgery, where should the waterproof sheet go?

options.A: Draped vertically over the bedside metal railings
options.B: Wrapped tightly around the patient's head pillow
options.C: Across the middle third of the mattress
options.D: Spread neatly over the bottom foot of the bed

explanation: Placing the waterproof sheet across the middle third protects the mattress from potential surgical drainage, bleeding, or vomit. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the most common sign reported by patients experiencing a pulmonary embolism?

options.A: Complete loss of vision in both eyes
options.B: A dull ache radiating down the left arm
options.C: Severe swelling in both ankles and feet
options.D: Sudden and unexplained shortness of breath

explanation: Sudden, unexplained shortness of breath is the main warning sign that should immediately make a nurse think of a pulmonary embolism. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T9#BMP125_U2_T9_h4)

question: A preterm baby boy is born at 32 weeks, and his scrotal sacs feel empty and cannot be felt. What is the best initial action for the midwife?

options.A: Document the finding and monitor during routine postnatal visits
options.B: Perform an immediate surgical repositioning procedure
options.C: Administer high-dose testosterone injections
options.D: Tell the mother the condition is permanent and untreatable

explanation: Many preterm infants experience delayed descent that corrects itself over the first few months, so monitoring is the appropriate step. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body have a higher metabolic rate?

options.A: To support the growing placenta and baby
options.B: To make up for less lung capacity late in pregnancy
options.C: To prevent excess nitrogen in the blood
options.D: To cool down the mother's body temperature

explanation: The developing baby and placenta need constant energy and support, which increases the mother's overall oxygen use. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman choose to pass a nearby clinic and travel further to another one?

options.A: Distant facilities always offer free medications regardless of type
options.B: She may feel the distant facility is more welcoming or affordable
options.C: Primary health care guidelines strictly require traveling past the first facility
options.D: Government policy bans women from using their closest health post

explanation: Accessibility includes how acceptable and affordable a clinic feels. Clients will travel further if local services lack a welcoming environment or fair pricing. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h1)

question: A mother with severe asthma is experiencing a heavy postpartum hemorrhage that is not responding to initial drugs. Which medication should the team avoid?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Carboprost
options.D: Tranexamic acid

explanation: Carboprost can cause the airways to narrow, making it unsafe for patients with a history of asthma. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does typing an entire email sentence in capital letters usually signify online?

options.A: Making the text easier to read for older supervisors
options.B: Indicating that the email is completely secure
options.C: Highlighting that the message contains financial data
options.D: Shouting or raising your voice at the reader

explanation: In internet communication, writing in all caps is treated as shouting, which can sound aggressive in professional messages. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T3#BMP123_U4_T3_h3)

question: A pregnant woman presents with chronic diarrhea, severe fatigue, and pale bulky stools that float. Which condition should a midwife suspect?

options.A: Urinary tract infection
options.B: Malabsorption syndrome
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: Fatty floating stools and fatigue point toward an inability to absorb nutrients and fats properly. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T3#BMP121_U2_T3_h8)

question: When should an induction of labor be planned for a patient on therapeutic low molecular weight heparin?

options.A: At least twenty-four hours after the final heparin injection
options.B: Immediately after the morning dose of heparin is administered
options.C: While the patient is at peak anticoagulation effect from heparin
options.D: Six hours before the next scheduled subcutaneous heparin dose

explanation: Waiting a full day after the last dose lets the drug wear off enough to keep bleeding risks low during childbirth. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T7#BMP213_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why are pelvic floor exercises recommended to women after a perineal repair?

options.A: To restore muscle strength and improve long-term pelvic support
options.B: To stop postpartum bleeding from the uterus within one hour
options.C: To prevent the baby from developing neonatal jaundice
options.D: To make the skin of the perineum heal with a lighter color

explanation: Targeted pelvic floor exercises improve blood circulation to the area and help regain muscle tone after childbirth. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is a key indicator that a bandage has been applied too tightly and is cutting off blood flow?

options.A: A slight increase in the client's normal appetite
options.B: The bandage fabric changing its original color
options.C: The patient feeling warm and relaxed on the bed
options.D: Numbness, tingling, or coldness in the fingers or toes

explanation: Nerves and blood vessels suffer when compressed, leading to cold digits, tingling sensations, or numbness distal to the bandage. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T4#BMP120_U3_T4_h6)

question: How does lignocaine stop pain signals from traveling along a nerve?

options.A: Stimulating local opioid receptors to block pain perception
options.B: Increasing potassium movement out of the cell completely
options.C: Destroying the myelin sheath surrounding the nerve fibre
options.D: Blocking sodium channels to prevent nerve depolarisation

explanation: Lignocaine works by blocking sodium channels, which stops the electrical signals the nerve needs to send pain messages to the brain. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T6#BMP213_U2_T6_h2)

question: A patient has a newly created AV fistula in the left arm. What vital daily assessment should be performed on this arm?

options.A: Check for a strong radial pulse and cool skin tone
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet to speed up maturation
options.C: Palpate for a thrill and auscultate for a bruit
options.D: Measure blood pressure using the left arm cuff

explanation: Checking for a physical thrill (vibration) and listening for a bruit (swooshing sound) confirms that blood is flowing freely through the access. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T8#BMP216_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do midwives check if a drug is safe for the baby before a breastfeeding mother takes it?

options.A: Maternal medications alter the nutritional value of milk
options.B: Newborns metabolize all drugs faster than adults
options.C: Breastfeeding stops completely if drugs are given
options.D: Many drugs can pass through breastmilk to the baby

explanation: Substances in the mother's bloodstream can pass into breastmilk and expose the nursing infant to the drug's effects. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h1)

question: A patient scheduled for a left leg amputation looks terrified and refuses to speak. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Tell the patient that worrying will only make recovery harder
options.B: Call the surgeon to cancel the operation right away
options.C: Sit quietly with the patient and offer a listening ear
options.D: Insist that the patient signs the consent form immediately

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space allows the patient to express overwhelming emotions and builds trust with the nursing team. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the main job of fascicles inside a skeletal muscle?

options.A: They anchor the muscle tendons directly to the bone surface.
options.B: They group individual muscle fibers together within perimysium.
options.C: They store calcium ions needed for muscle shortening.
options.D: They produce ATP molecules for resting muscle tissue.

explanation: Fascicles are bundles of muscle fibers enclosed by the perimysium to help organize the muscle structure. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h1)

question: What part of the reproductive system does a midwife check during a vaginal exam to see how labor is progressing?

options.A: The cervix
options.B: The clitoris
options.C: The uterine fundus
options.D: The fallopian tubes

explanation: Measuring how much the cervix has opened helps midwives track how labor is advancing. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h1)

question: How must Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) be released from the hypothalamus to keep the pituitary working normally?

options.A: In response to high uterine pressure
options.B: Only once per menstrual cycle
options.C: In a continuous steady stream
options.D: In distinct pulses

explanation: Pulsatile secretion prevents receptor downregulation, which happens when pituitary cells are exposed to constant, uninterrupted hormone levels. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h3)

question: A midwife notices a doctor using complex medical terms that a frightened patient does not understand. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Advise the patient to discharge themselves immediately without treatment
options.B: Break down the explanation into simple terms and ensure the patient understands
options.C: Tell the patient to stop asking questions and obey the medical team
options.D: Ignore the situation because doctors are solely responsible for communication

explanation: The midwife acts as an advocate by ensuring true informed consent through simple, clear explanations. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary reason for advising a mother with mastitis to continue breastfeeding?

options.A: It prevents the baby from developing infant colic
options.B: It stops the mother's milk supply from drying up permanently
options.C: It helps drain the affected ducts and resolves the condition
options.D: It ensures the baby's daily vitamin intake is maintained

explanation: Removing milk frequently is the most effective way to clear the blockage and heal the inflamed tissue. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T6#BMP214_U3_T6_h5)

question: What should a midwife do first if a mother develops a bad rash after using a prescribed cream?

options.A: Stop the medication, wash the area gently with water, and report the reaction.
options.B: Tell the mother to ignore it until her next scheduled clinic appointment next month.
options.C: Scrub the affected skin vigorously with harsh antiseptic soap and alcohol.
options.D: Apply a thicker layer of the same ointment to cover the new rash completely.

explanation: Washing the area stops further exposure to the drug, and reporting the reaction ensures the patient gets a safer alternative. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T4#BMP120_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is a classic sign of developing shock in an emergency patient?

options.A: Deep, relaxed breathing and quiet sleep
options.B: Warm, pink skin with a very slow pulse
options.C: Cold, clammy skin with a fast pulse
options.D: High alertness and a very low blood pressure

explanation: When the body goes into shock, blood is redirected to vital organs, making the skin cool and the heart beat faster. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T1#BMP110_U7_T1_h5)

question: What is a common sign of weak pelvic floor muscles during pregnancy?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Severe pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Stress urinary incontinence
options.D: Premature rupture of membranes

explanation: When the pelvic floor muscles are weak, the weight of the pregnancy can cause urine to leak when coughing, sneezing, or laughing. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T6#BMP111_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why do we keep patient records in the maternity unit?

options.A: Meeting personal journaling needs
options.B: Reducing the cost of medical supplies
options.C: Providing a permanent legal account of care
options.D: Fulfilling hospital administrative quotas

explanation: Records serve as a permanent history that protects both the patient and the midwife while guiding ongoing care. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h1)

question: How do community mobilization strategies improve antenatal care attendance in rural areas?

options.A: By eliminating all transportation costs
options.B: By forcing husbands to pay fines
options.C: By building trust through local leaders and addressing cultural fears
options.D: By replacing trained midwives

explanation: Working with community leaders helps clear up misunderstandings and encourages local women to trust and use the nearby health facility. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T2#BMP126_U1_T2_h4)

question: What daily intake defines trace minerals in the human body?

options.A: More than five hundred milligrams
options.B: Between one and two grams
options.C: Exactly ten grams
options.D: Less than 100 milligrams

explanation: Micro minerals are needed in tiny amounts, specifically under 100 milligrams daily, unlike macro minerals which are needed in larger quantities. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why must a midwife assess scene safety before helping a victim?

options.A: To calculate the cost of medical supplies needed
options.B: To make sure the police write an official report
options.C: To prevent the rescuer from becoming another casualty
options.D: To find out who caused the accident

explanation: If the environment remains dangerous, the healthcare worker may also get injured, leaving fewer people to help. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T8#BMP110_U7_T8_h3)

question: Why is a heart attack also called a type of ischaemic heart disease?

options.A: It develops because the lungs fail to filter enough oxygen into blood.
options.B: It results directly from a long-standing infection in the heart valves.
options.C: It only happens when the heart beats too fast during physical rest.
options.D: It is caused by a permanent lack of blood supply to the heart tissue.

explanation: The term ischaemia means a shortage of blood supply, which is the root cause of both chest pain and heart attacks. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T4#BMP125_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is keeping emergency equipment in a centralized, known location vital during a crisis?

options.A: It reduces the total number of nurses needed on duty
options.B: It ensures that equipment never breaks down or requires repairs
options.C: It prevents patients from touching the equipment
options.D: It minimizes time wasted searching for tools during an emergency

explanation: In obstetric emergencies, every second counts, and knowing exactly where supplies are saves critical time. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h4)

question: What are two very common side effects after receiving Syntometrine?

options.A: Excessive hair loss and rash
options.B: Lower limb swelling and edema
options.C: Nausea and vomiting
options.D: Severe drowsiness and sleep

explanation: Many patients feel nauseous or vomit shortly after receiving Syntometrine due to how ergot medicines affect the brain. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is a multi-disciplinary health team approach necessary in secondary health facilities?

options.A: Hospital management boards require all staff to share administrative duties equally
options.B: Different specialists are needed to manage complex medical and surgical conditions effectively
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to write patient care reports
options.D: It ensures that doctors do not have to work night shifts in the wards

explanation: Complex health issues require combined expertise from doctors, midwives, pharmacists, and lab scientists to achieve the best patient outcome. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following devices is NOT used to support body alignment?

options.A: Intravenous infusion pole
options.B: Footboard
options.C: Trochanter roll
options.D: Sandbag

explanation: An intravenous infusion pole is used to hang fluid bags, whereas trochanter rolls, footboards, and sandbags are direct body alignment support devices. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h4)

question: A non-pregnant woman has a calculated Body Mass Index of 28.5. How should a midwife classify this result?

options.A: Severely obese
options.B: Underweight
options.C: Normal weight
options.D: Overweight

explanation: A BMI reading between 25.0 and 29.9 falls into the overweight category. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T3#BMP110_U6_T3_h6)

question: What is the main job of gap junctions in the heart muscle?

options.A: Allowing free passage of ions for rapid electrical communication between cells
options.B: Anchoring the actin and myosin filaments directly to the cell membrane
options.C: Secreting hormones that regulate overall systemic blood pressure
options.D: Providing strong mechanical anchorage to prevent cells from tearing apart

explanation: Gap junctions create pathways for electrical signals to spread swiftly from cell to cell across the heart wall. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h3)

question: About how many of the body's total platelets are stored in a normal spleen?

options.A: One-third
options.B: Three-quarters
options.C: One-half
options.D: One-tenth

explanation: The spleen keeps about one-third of the body's platelets in reserve, ready to be released if bleeding happens. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h5)

question: A woman is admitted in early latent labor at 2 cm dilation requesting immediate pain relief with morphine. What is the most appropriate action for the midwife?

options.A: Delay administration because giving it too early can slow down labor progress.
options.B: Transfer her straight to the operating theatre for an emergency caesarean section.
options.C: Refuse all forms of pain relief until she reaches full 10 cm dilation.
options.D: Administer a double intravenous dose immediately to speed up her dilation.

explanation: Giving systemic opioids during the latent phase before active labor is established can interfere with uterine contractions and prolong labor. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which organ does the superior mesenteric vein primarily drain?

options.A: The brainstem
options.B: The urinary bladder
options.C: The left kidney
options.D: The small intestine

explanation: The superior mesenteric vein collects nutrient-laden blood specifically from the small intestine and parts of the large intestine. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T19#BMP111_U5_T19_h2)

question: Where should the safety box for sharp objects ideally be positioned during a busy labor ward shift?

options.A: Underneath the patient's bed away from active clinical traffic
options.B: Inside the main utility room down the hospital corridor
options.C: Right at the point of use close to where the procedure occurs
options.D: Locked inside the senior midwife's office desk drawer

explanation: Placing sharps boxes close to where injections and procedures happen prevents midwives from carrying exposed needles across the room. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h4)

question: What major complication is prevented by making sure bed sheets are free of wrinkles?

options.A: Pressure sores
options.B: Joint stiffness
options.C: Fungal infections
options.D: Muscle cramps

explanation: Wrinkles create constant friction and pressure against fragile skin, which quickly leads to the development of pressure sores. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h6)

question: A male partner insists on answering all questions for his pregnant wife and refuses to leave the consultation room. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: A medical requirement mandated by the national health ministry
options.B: Potential controlling behavior and a red flag for possible gender-based violence
options.C: Standard supportive behavior expected of all expectant fathers
options.D: An indication that the patient has excellent mental health

explanation: An overly dominant partner who refuses to leave the patient alone often uses isolation and control, which are core indicators of abuse. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why are the ovaries considered both exocrine and endocrine organs?

options.A: They produce digestive enzymes alongside monthly menstrual blood flow
options.B: They filter waste products from the pelvis while storing urine temporarily
options.C: They control both voluntary leg movements and involuntary uterine contractions
options.D: They release egg cells and also secrete reproductive hormones into the bloodstream

explanation: Ovaries produce gametes (ova) and secrete key hormones like estrogen and progesterone directly into the blood supply. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T2#BMP210_U2_T2_h5)

question: What does a high-pitched whistling sound, known as stridor, indicate in a newly arrived surgical patient?

options.A: Normal recovery from muscle relaxants
options.B: Partial upper airway obstruction
options.C: Excessive fluid intake during the operation
options.D: Adequate oxygen saturation levels

explanation: Stridor is a turbulent sound caused by a narrowed or partially blocked upper airway that requires prompt attention. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T3#BMP120_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main role of the skin in regulating body temperature?

options.A: It blocks all heat exchange between the body and the air.
options.B: It detects changes in the environment and helps the body respond.
options.C: It produces all the heat needed to keep internal organs warm.
options.D: It controls the nervous system signals that dictate metabolism.

explanation: The skin contains sensors and blood vessels that help sense outside temperatures and adjust how much heat the body loses or keeps. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T5#BMP111_U4_T5_h1)

question: Where should the midwife direct pressure when performing the Johnson maneuver?

options.A: Outward against the lateral pelvic walls
options.B: Upward toward the umbilicus
options.C: Downward toward the perineal floor
options.D: Forward against the pubic bone

explanation: Pushing the fundus upward along the vaginal axis toward the umbilicus stretches the ligaments and helps pop the uterus back through the cervix. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T2#BMP311_U4_T2_h5)

question: How many quadrants is the abdominopelvic cavity divided into for general clinical assessments?

options.A: Six
options.B: Nine
options.C: Two
options.D: Four

explanation: Crossing the abdomen with one vertical and one horizontal line creates four simple quadrants. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T1#BMP111_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why do individuals with darker skin tones have more natural protection against ultraviolet (UV) radiation?

options.A: Their melanocytes produce more melanin and larger pigment packages
options.B: Idiopathically, they possess a higher total count of melanocytes
options.C: Their skin cells completely lack nuclei that UV rays can damage
options.D: Their outer skin layer is twice as thick as in lighter skin

explanation: Skin color differences depend on how much melanin is produced and how it is packaged, not the actual number of melanocytes. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h5)

question: How do the levator ani muscles help direct the mechanism of labor as the baby descends?

options.A: They contract forcefully to push the baby out without maternal effort
options.B: They seal the cervix shut until crowning occurs
options.C: They absorb all amniotic fluid to keep the birth canal dry
options.D: Their slope helps guide the fetal head to rotate forward

explanation: The downward and forward slope of the resting pelvic floor acts like a slide, helping the presenting part rotate correctly toward the front of the pelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T7#BMP210_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the appropriate response when a patient mentions a traditional health belief that is harmless?

options.A: Refuse to treat her until she abandons her cultural heritage.
options.B: Report her to local law enforcement authorities immediately.
options.C: Scold the patient publicly to stop her from talking about it.
options.D: Respect the harmless belief while providing safe care.

explanation: Midwives practice cultural competence by respecting harmless traditions while addressing only those practices that threaten health. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why do medicines applied to the vagina absorb much faster than those put on regular skin?

options.A: Mucous membranes produce oils that dissolve all types of drug molecules.
options.B: Vaginal mucous membranes lack a tough stratum corneum and have rich blood supplies.
options.C: Vaginal tissues are always warmer than the external skin surface.
options.D: The skin on the body has a thicker layer of fat underneath it.

explanation: Without a tough outer layer, and with a rich network of blood vessels nearby, topical treatments can enter the bloodstream very quickly through mucous membranes. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T4#BMP120_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why are veins commonly called capacitance vessels?

options.A: They generate their own electrical impulses like the heart
options.B: They contain thick muscular walls to store oxygen
options.C: They expand easily to store large amounts of blood
options.D: They carry high-pressure blood directly to the lungs

explanation: Capacitance refers to the ability of veins to stretch and hold a large volume of blood at low pressure. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T16#BMP111_U5_T16_h4)

question: What happens to the diaphragm during pregnancy that affects how a woman breathes?

options.A: It is pushed upward by the growing uterus
options.B: It moves downward into the abdominal cavity
options.C: It becomes completely paralyzed due to hormones
options.D: It thickens significantly to pump more air

explanation: The expanding uterus takes up space in the abdomen and gently pushes the diaphragm upward, which naturally reduces lung capacity. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T8#BMP125_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why does anaerobic energy production lead to quicker muscle fatigue than aerobic respiration?

question: Why is family involvement important in the supportive care of a mother suffering from mastitis?
